name: Psalms
sourceNote:
Source and method. The Psalms are translated from the Hebrew Masoretic Text as given in the Westminster Leningrad Codex (Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible), compared with the Greek Septuagint (Brenton) and, where they bear on the text, the Dead Sea Scrolls. Significant differences are footnoted. Where the written Hebrew text (ketiv) and the traditional reading (qere) differ, the qere is followed unless a note says otherwise; only cases that affect the sense are noted. Poetry is set out line by line as the Hebrew parallelism falls.

Verse numbers. This translation uses the standard English verse numbers. In the Hebrew Bible a psalm's title (superscription) is counted as verse 1, or as verses 1–2 in Psalms 51, 52, 54 and 60; so in most titled psalms the Hebrew verse numbers run one (or two) higher than the English. Here the titles are printed above each psalm. They are ancient and are part of the Hebrew text, but most scholars think they were added after the psalms were written.

Numbering of the psalms. The Greek Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate (and Bibles based on them, such as the older Catholic versions) number the psalms differently: Hebrew 9–10 are one psalm (Greek 9), so Hebrew 11–113 are Greek 10–112; Hebrew 114–115 are one psalm (Greek 113); Hebrew 116 is two (Greek 114–115); Hebrew 117–146 are Greek 116–145; Hebrew 147 is two (Greek 146–147); Psalms 148–150 agree. The Greek also has a Psalm 151, which is not in the Hebrew Bible; it will be given with the Apocrypha.

The five books. From early times the Psalter has been divided into five books, each closing with a blessing of God (a doxology): Book One, Psalms 1–41; Book Two, 42–72; Book Three, 73–89; Book Four, 90–106; Book Five, 107–150. Psalm 150 serves as the closing doxology of the whole.

Dead Sea Scrolls. About forty Psalms scrolls or fragments were found at Qumran, more than for any other book. The largest, the Great Psalms Scroll from Cave 11 (11QPs-a, copied in the first century AD), contains parts of some 40 biblical psalms from Psalms 93–150, in an order that often differs from the Hebrew Bible, together with other poems, among them a Hebrew form of Psalm 151. Scholars debate whether it is a variant Psalter or a liturgical collection. Important readings are noted where they occur.

Names of God. The divine name YHWH is rendered Yahweh. The short form Yah is kept as Yah. Hallelujah is Hebrew halelu-yah, "praise Yah." Adonai is rendered Lord, Elohim God, El God (or "the Mighty One"), Elyon the Most High, and YHWH Tsebaoth "Yahweh of Armies." Note that Psalms 42–83 (the "Elohistic Psalter") mostly use Elohim where other psalms use Yahweh.

Musical and liturgical terms. Many words in the titles (Maskil, Miktam, Shiggaion, Sheminith, Gittith, and others) and the word Selah within the psalms are of uncertain meaning; they are kept in Hebrew form with notes. Acrostic psalms, whose lines or stanzas begin with the successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet, are marked in notes (Psalms 9–10, 25, 34, 37, 111, 112, 119, 145); Psalm 119 gives the Hebrew letter of each eight-verse stanza.

verses.text:
but his delight is in the law{b} of Yahweh,
and on his law he meditates{c} day and night.

He will be like a tree planted beside streams of water,
which yields its fruit in its time;
its leaf also does not wither,
and whatever he does prospers.

Not so the wicked!
They are like the chaff that the wind drives away.

Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment,
nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.

For Yahweh knows the way of the righteous,
but the way of the wicked will perish.

notes.text: Or “Happy is the one.” Hebrew ’ashre, “O the happiness of,” opens Psalm 1 and closes Psalm 2 (2:12), so that the two psalms frame an introduction to the whole Psalter. “The man” here stands for any person who lives this way.
Hebrew torah, “instruction, teaching”: God’s word as a whole, not only the commandments.
Hebrew hagah, to murmur or recite in a low voice; reading aloud and pondering.

verses.text:
Why do the nations rage,{a}
and the peoples mutter empty plans?

“Let us tear their bonds apart,
and cast their ropes away from us!”

The One enthroned in the heavens laughs;
the Lord{c} mocks them.

Then he will speak to them in his anger,
and terrify them in his fury:

“But I—I have set my king
on Zion, my holy mountain.”

Ask it of me, and I will give you the nations for your heritage,
and the farthest ends of the earth for your own.

You will break them with a rod of iron;{e}
you will smash them like a potter’s jar.”

Now therefore, you kings, be wise;
be warned, you judges of the earth.

Serve Yahweh with fear,
and rejoice with trembling.

Kiss the son,{f} lest he be angry and you perish on the way,
for his anger is quickly kindled.
Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

notes.text: Or “gather in tumult.” Acts 4:25–26 quotes verses 1–2 from the Greek.
Hebrew mashiakh, “anointed one,” the king anointed with oil; the word from which “Messiah” comes. The New Testament reads this psalm of Christ (Acts 13:33; Hebrews 1:5; 5:5).
Hebrew Adonai, “Lord, Master,” a title of God distinct from the divine name Yahweh. It is rendered “Lord” throughout this translation.
Hebrew “I have begotten you,” the language of the king’s installation as God’s son (compare 2 Samuel 7:14).
The Septuagint, reading the same consonants with other vowels, has “You will shepherd them with a rod of iron,” the form quoted in Revelation 2:27; 12:5; 19:15.

The Hebrew is difficult. “Son” here is bar, the Aramaic word (Hebrew uses ben, as in verse 7). Some take the line as “Kiss purely,” or “Do homage in purity”; the Septuagint has “Take hold of instruction,” and the Latin Vulgate (Jerome) “Embrace discipline,” though Jerome elsewhere rendered “worship purely.” Kissing the hand or feet was a sign of submission to a king.

chapters.title: A psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.{a}

verses.text:
Yahweh, how many are my foes!
Many are rising up against me;

But you, Yahweh, are a shield around me,
my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.

With my voice I cry to Yahweh,
and he answers me from his holy mountain.
Selah

I lay down and slept;
I woke, for Yahweh sustains me.

I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people
who have set themselves against me all around.

notes.text: See 2 Samuel 15–18. In the Hebrew Bible a psalm’s title is counted as verse 1 (or verses 1–2), so the Hebrew verse numbers of titled psalms usually run one higher than the English numbers used here.

Selah occurs 71 times in the Psalms and three times in Habakkuk 3. Its meaning is unknown; it is probably a musical or liturgical direction, perhaps calling for a pause, an interlude, or a raising of the voice. The Septuagint renders it diapsalma, “interlude.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader:{a} with stringed instruments.{b} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
You sons of men,{d} how long will my honor be turned to shame?
How long will you love emptiness and seek after lies?
Selah

Know that Yahweh has set apart the faithful one{e} for himself;
Yahweh hears when I call to him.

Offer sacrifices of righteousness,
and put your trust in Yahweh.

Many are saying, “Who will show us good?”
Lift up the light of your face upon us, Yahweh!

You have put gladness in my heart,
more than when their grain and new wine abound.

In peace I will both lie down and sleep,
for you alone, Yahweh, make me dwell in safety.

notes.text: Hebrew lamnatseakh, perhaps “for the leader,” “for the director of music”; it heads 55 psalms. The Septuagint takes it as “for the end.”
Hebrew neginot.
Hebrew “you made room for me.”
Or “You people of rank”; Hebrew bene ’ish, which may mean men of standing.
Hebrew khasid, one devoted to God and loyal in covenant love (khesed).
Or “Be angry.” The Septuagint has “Be angry, and do not sin,” quoted in Ephesians 4:26.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: for the flutes.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Give ear to my words, Yahweh;
consider my sighing.{b}

Listen to the sound of my cry, my King and my God,
for to you I pray.

Yahweh, in the morning you hear my voice;
in the morning I lay my case before you{c} and keep watch.

For you are not a God who takes pleasure in wickedness;
evil cannot dwell with you.

The arrogant cannot stand in your sight;
you hate all who do evil.

You destroy those who speak lies;
the man of bloodshed and deceit Yahweh abhors.

But as for me, by the greatness of your covenant love{d} I will come into your house;
in awe of you I will bow down toward your holy temple.

Lead me, Yahweh, in your righteousness because of those who lie in wait for me;
make your way straight before me.

Hold them guilty, O God;
let them fall by their own schemes.
For their many transgressions thrust them out,
for they have rebelled against you.

For you bless the righteous, Yahweh;
you surround him with favor as with a shield.

notes.text: Hebrew nekhilot, probably “flutes”; the meaning is uncertain.
Or “my murmuring,” “my meditation.”
Or “I prepare a sacrifice for you”; the verb is used of setting out an offering or arranging words.
Hebrew khesed, God’s loyal, covenant-keeping love and kindness; a key word of the Psalms (it occurs about 130 times), rendered “covenant love” in this translation.
Paul quotes this line in Romans 3:13.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: with stringed instruments, on the eighth.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, do not rebuke me in your anger,
nor discipline me in your wrath.

Be gracious to me, Yahweh, for I am languishing;
heal me, Yahweh, for my bones are shaken.

My soul also is greatly shaken;
but you, Yahweh—how long?

Turn, Yahweh, rescue my soul;
save me because of your covenant love.

For in death there is no remembrance of you;
in Sheol{b} who will give you thanks?

My eye is wasted with sorrow;
it has grown old because of all my adversaries.

Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity,
for Yahweh has heard the sound of my weeping.

Yahweh has heard my plea;
Yahweh accepts my prayer.

All my enemies will be ashamed and greatly shaken;
they will turn back and be put to shame in a moment.

notes.text: Hebrew ’al hasheminit, perhaps an instrument of eight strings, or a lower octave; the meaning is uncertain. This is the first of seven psalms that the church has long called the Penitential Psalms (6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143).
Sheol is the Hebrew name for the realm of the dead, the grave or underworld.

chapters.title: A shiggaion{a} of David, which he sang to Yahweh concerning the words of Cush, a Benjaminite.{b}

verses.text:
Yahweh my God, in you I take refuge;
save me from all who pursue me, and deliver me,

lest like a lion they tear my soul apart,
dragging me off, with none to deliver.

Yahweh my God, if I have done this,
if there is wrong in my hands,

if I have paid back evil to the one at peace with me,
or stripped my adversary without cause,

let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it,
and trample my life to the ground,
and lay my glory in the dust.
Selah

Let the assembly of the peoples gather around you,
and over it return on high.

Let the evil of the wicked come to an end,
but establish the righteous—
you who test hearts and minds,{d} O righteous God.

My shield is with God,
who saves the upright in heart.

God is a righteous judge,
and a God who is indignant every day.

If a man does not repent, God will sharpen his sword;
he has bent his bow and made it ready.

He has prepared for himself weapons of death;
he makes his arrows fiery shafts.

Look, the wicked man conceives iniquity;
he is pregnant with mischief and gives birth to lies.

He digs a pit and scoops it out,
and falls himself into the hole he made.

His mischief returns upon his own head,
and his violence comes down on his own skull.

I will give thanks to Yahweh for his righteousness,
and I will sing praise to the name of Yahweh, the Most High.{e}

notes.text: Hebrew shiggayon, a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps a lament or an impassioned song (compare Habakkuk 3:1).
Cush is otherwise unknown; perhaps an ally of Saul from Saul’s tribe of Benjamin.
Or “awake, my God”; the Septuagint has “awake, O Lord my God.”
Hebrew “hearts and kidneys,” the seat of thought and of the deepest feelings.
Hebrew Elyon, “Most High,” a title of God (compare Genesis 14:18–22).

chapters.title: For the choir leader: on the gittith.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers,
the moon and the stars, which you have set in place,

what is man that you remember him,
and the son of man{e} that you care for him?

Yet you have made him only a little less than God,{f}
and with glory and honor you crown him.

You make him ruler over the works of your hands;
you have put all things under his feet:

sheep and oxen, all of them,
and also the beasts of the field,

the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea,
all that travel the paths of the seas.

Yahweh, our Lord,
how majestic is your name in all the earth!

notes.text: Hebrew ’al haggittit, perhaps an instrument or tune from Gath, or a song for the winepress (Hebrew gat); the meaning is uncertain.
Here “Lord” is Hebrew ’adon, “master, sovereign,” the ordinary word for a lord, used here of God.
The Hebrew of this line is difficult; literally perhaps “which, give your splendor upon the heavens.”
The Septuagint has “you have prepared praise,” the form quoted in Matthew 21:16.
Or “what is a human being… and a mortal.” Hebrew ’enosh and ben ’adam are both words for humankind. Hebrews 2:6–8 reads verses 4–6 of Jesus.
Hebrew ’elohim, which can mean God or heavenly beings; the Septuagint has “angels,” as quoted in Hebrews 2:7.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: on Muth-labben.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
I will give thanks to Yahweh with my whole heart;
I will recount all your wonderful deeds.

I will be glad and exult in you;
I will sing praise to your name, O Most High.

When my enemies turn back,
they stumble and perish before you.

For you have maintained my right and my cause;
you sit on the throne, a righteous judge.

You have rebuked the nations; you have destroyed the wicked;
you have blotted out their name forever and ever.

But Yahweh is seated as king forever;
he has set up his throne for judgment.

And he will judge the world in righteousness;
he will judge the peoples with equity.

Yahweh will be a high refuge for the crushed,
a high refuge in times of distress.

And those who know your name will trust in you,
for you, Yahweh, have not forsaken those who seek you.

Sing praises to Yahweh, who dwells in Zion!
Tell among the peoples his deeds!

For the one who requires blood remembers them;
he has not forgotten the outcry of the humble.{b}

Be gracious to me, Yahweh!
See my affliction from those who hate me,
you who lift me up from the gates of death,

The nations have sunk down into the pit they dug;
their own foot is caught in the net they hid.

The wicked shall turn back to Sheol,
all the nations who forget God.

For the needy will not always be forgotten,
nor the hope of the afflicted{e} perish forever.

Arise, Yahweh! Let not man prevail;
let the nations be judged before you.

notes.text: Hebrew ’al-mut labben, perhaps “on the death of the son,” the name of a tune; the meaning is uncertain. Psalms 9 and 10 together form a single acrostic poem, each pair of verses beginning with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet, though the pattern is broken in places. Psalm 10 has no title, and the Septuagint and Vulgate treat 9–10 as one psalm (their Psalm 9); from there until Psalm 147 their numbering runs one behind the Hebrew (see the note on the numbering at the end of the book).
So the qere; the ketiv has “the afflicted.” The two Hebrew words, ‘aniyyim and ‘anawim, are often interchanged in the Psalms.
That is, the city of Jerusalem, pictured as a young woman.
Hebrew higgayon, perhaps a musical interlude or a meditative murmur (compare 19:14; 92:3).
So the qere; the ketiv has “the humble.”

verses.text:
Why, Yahweh, do you stand far off?
Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?

In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the afflicted;
let them be caught in the schemes they have devised.

For the wicked boasts of the desire of his soul,
and the greedy one curses and spurns Yahweh.{a}

In his haughtiness the wicked does not seek him;
“There is no God” is the sum of all his schemes.

He says in his heart, “I will not be moved;
throughout all generations I will not meet adversity.”

His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and oppression;{b}
under his tongue are mischief and iniquity.

He crouches, he bows down,
and the helpless fall by his might.{c}

He says in his heart, “God has forgotten;
he has hidden his face; he will never see it.”

Arise, Yahweh! O God, raise your hand;
do not forget the lowly.{d}

Why does the wicked spurn God
and say in his heart, “You will not call to account”?

Break the arm of the wicked and the evildoer;
seek out his wickedness until you find none.

Yahweh is King forever and ever;
the nations have perished from his land.

Yahweh, you have heard the desire of the humble;
you will strengthen their heart; you will incline your ear

to do justice for the fatherless and the oppressed,
so that man, who is of the earth, may no more cause terror.

notes.text: Or “and blesses the greedy one, and spurns Yahweh.” The Hebrew is uncertain; “curses” translates “blesses,” which may be a scribal euphemism.
Paul quotes this line in Romans 3:14.
The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
So the qere; the ketiv has “the afflicted.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader. Of David.{a}

verses.text:
When the foundations are torn down,
what can the righteous do?

Yahweh puts the righteous to the test,
but the wicked and the lover of violence his soul hates.

On the wicked he will rain snares;{c}
fire and sulfur and a scorching wind will be the portion of their cup.

For Yahweh is righteous and loves acts of righteousness;
the upright shall gaze upon his face.

notes.text: Or “By David,” “For David,” or “Belonging to David.” The Hebrew preposition le- in the titles can mark authorship, dedication, or a collection associated with David.
So the qere; the ketiv has a plural verb, “Flee, you people.”
Or, with a slight change, “coals of fire.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader: on the eighth. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Save, Yahweh, for the godly one is no more;
the faithful have vanished from among the children of man.

Each one speaks falsehood with his neighbor;
with smooth lips and a double heart they speak.

May Yahweh cut off all smooth lips,
the tongue that talks of great things,

those who say, “By our tongue we shall be strong;
our lips are with us—who is lord over us?”

You, Yahweh, will keep them;
you will guard him{c} from this generation forever.

On every side the wicked prowl,
when vileness is exalted among the children of man.

notes.text: Or “that he pants for”; or “from the one who puffs at him.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
The meaning of the Hebrew phrase is uncertain.
Or “guard us” (so some Hebrew manuscripts and the Septuagint).

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
How long, Yahweh? Will you forget me forever?
How long will you hide your face from me?

How long must I take counsel in my soul,
with sorrow in my heart all the day?
How long shall my enemy be exalted over me?

Look on me and answer me, Yahweh my God;
give light to my eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death,

lest my enemy say, “I have overcome him,”
lest my foes rejoice because I am shaken.

But as for me, I have trusted in your covenant love;
my heart shall rejoice in your salvation.

I will sing to Yahweh,
because he has dealt generously with me.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. Of David.{a}

verses.text:
Yahweh looks down from heaven on the children of man,
to see whether there is anyone who understands,
anyone who seeks after God.

Do all the workers of iniquity have no knowledge,
who eat up my people as they eat bread,
and do not call upon Yahweh?

There they shall be in terror, terror indeed,
for God is in the company of the righteous.

You would put to shame the plans of the afflicted,
but Yahweh is his refuge.

Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion!
When Yahweh restores the fortunes of his people,
let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

notes.text: Psalm 14 appears again, with small differences, as Psalm 53, where God (Elohim) stands in place of Yahweh.
Hebrew nabal, one who is morally and spiritually senseless, not merely unintelligent (compare Nabal in 1 Samuel 25:25).
Paul quotes verses 1–3 in Romans 3:10–12. Some Septuagint manuscripts add here the lines that Paul quotes in Romans 3:13–18.

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, who may sojourn in your tent?
Who may dwell on your holy mountain?

The one who walks blamelessly and does what is right,
and speaks truth in his heart;

notes.text: Lending at interest to a fellow Israelite in need was forbidden by the law (Exodus 22:25; Leviticus 25:35–37; Deuteronomy 23:19–20).

chapters.title: A miktam{a} of David.

verses.text: Preserve me, O God, for in you I take refuge.

I said{b} to Yahweh, “You are my Lord;
I have no good apart from you.”

As for the saints who are in the land,
they are the majestic ones, and all my delight is in them.{c}

Yahweh is my allotted portion and my cup;
you hold fast my lot.

My measured portion has fallen to me in lovely places;
indeed, my heritage is beautiful to me.

I will bless Yahweh, who gives me counsel;
even in the nights my inmost being{d} instructs me.

I have set Yahweh always before me;
because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.

So my heart rejoices and my glory{e} is glad;
my body too shall rest secure.

For you will not abandon my soul to Sheol,
nor let your faithful one{f} see the pit.{g}

notes.text: Hebrew miktam, a term of uncertain meaning, used in the titles of Psalms 16 and 56–60; perhaps “inscription” or “epigram.”
So the Septuagint and some Hebrew manuscripts; most Hebrew manuscripts have “You said,” addressed to the soul.
The Hebrew of verses 3 and 4 is difficult, and the sense is uncertain.
Hebrew “my kidneys.”
Or “my soul”; the Septuagint has “my tongue,” as quoted in Acts 2:26.
So the qere and many Hebrew manuscripts, with the ancient versions; the ketiv has “your faithful ones.”
Or “see corruption.” The Septuagint has “corruption,” the form quoted in Acts 2:27 and 13:35, where Peter and Paul apply verses 8–11 to the resurrection of Jesus.

chapters.title: A prayer of David.

verses.text:
Hear what is right, Yahweh; attend to my cry!
Give ear to my prayer from lips free of deceit!

Let my sentence go out from before you;
may your eyes see the things that are right.

As for the deeds of men, by the word of your lips
I have kept myself from the ways of the violent.

My steps have held fast to your paths;
my feet have not slipped.

I call upon you, for you will answer me, O God;
incline your ear to me; hear my words.

Show the wonders of your covenant love,
you who save by your right hand
those who seek refuge from their adversaries.

Keep me as the pupil of the eye;{a}
hide me in the shadow of your wings

from the wicked who assault me,
my deadly enemies who surround me.

They have closed up their unfeeling heart;{b}
with their mouth they speak arrogantly.

They have tracked us down; now they have surrounded us;{c}
they set their eyes to cast us to the ground.

He is like a lion that longs to rend its prey,
like a young lion crouching in secret places.

Arise, Yahweh, confront him, bring him down!
Deliver my soul from the wicked by your sword,

But I, in righteousness I shall see your face;
when I wake, your form will satisfy me.

notes.text: Hebrew “as the little man, the daughter of the eye,” referring to the small reflection one sees in another’s pupil.
Hebrew “their fat.”
So the qere; the ketiv has “surrounded me.”

So the qere (“your treasured things”); the ketiv has a different spelling of the same word. The sense of the verse is uncertain: it may describe the punishment stored up for the wicked, or the good things God gives his own.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. Of David the servant of Yahweh, who spoke to Yahweh the words of this song on the day when Yahweh delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.{a} He said:

verses.text: I love you, Yahweh, my strength.{b}

Yahweh is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer,
my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge,
my shield, and the horn{c} of my salvation, my high tower.

I call upon Yahweh, who is worthy to be praised,
and I am saved from my enemies.

The ropes of death wrapped around me;
the floods of destruction{d} overwhelmed me with terror;

the ropes of Sheol coiled about me;
the traps of death came upon me.

In my distress I called on Yahweh,
and to my God I cried out;
he heard my voice out of his temple,
and my cry for help before him reached his ears.

He bowed the heavens and came down;
thick darkness was under his feet.

He rode on a cherub and flew;
he soared on the wings of the wind.

He made darkness his covering, his canopy around him,
dark waters, thick clouds of the skies.

From the brightness before him
his thick clouds passed by,
hailstones and coals of fire.

He shot his arrows and scattered them;{f}
lightning bolts he hurled and threw them into confusion.

Then the channels of water were seen,
and the foundations of the world were laid bare
at your rebuke, Yahweh,
at the blast of the breath of your nostrils.

He reached down from on high, he took me;
he drew me out of many waters.

He delivered me from my strong enemy,
and from those who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.

They confronted me in the day of my calamity,
but Yahweh was my support.

He led me out into a wide, open place;
he rescued me because he took pleasure in me.

Yahweh dealt with me according to my righteousness;
according to the cleanness of my hands he repaid me.

For I have kept the ways of Yahweh,
and have not wickedly departed from my God.

For all his judgments were before me,
and his statutes I did not put away from me.

I was blameless before him,
and I kept myself from my iniquity.

So Yahweh has repaid me according to my righteousness,
according to the cleanness of my hands in his sight.

To the loyal you show yourself loyal;
to the man of integrity you show yourself whole;

to the pure you prove yourself pure,
but to the twisted you prove yourself crafty.

For a lowly people you save,
but proud eyes you humble.

For you light my lamp;
Yahweh my God lights up my darkness.

For by you I rush upon a raiding band,
and by my God I leap over a rampart.

For who is God, except Yahweh?
And who is a rock, except our God?—

the God who girds me with strength
and makes my way blameless.

He makes my feet like a doe’s feet
and makes me stand firm on the heights.

He teaches my hands to fight,
and my arms can draw a bow of bronze.

You have given me the shield of your salvation,
and your right hand has upheld me,
and your gentleness{g} has made me great.

You have widened the ground beneath my steps,
and my ankles have not slipped.

I chased my enemies and caught up with them;
I did not turn around till I had finished them.

I struck them through, so that they could not rise;
they fell under my feet.

For you girded me with strength for the battle;
you made those who rose against me bow down under me.

You made my enemies show me their backs,
and I wiped out those who hated me.

They cried for help, but there was none to save;
they cried to Yahweh, but he did not answer them.

I ground them like dust before the wind;
I poured them out like mire in the streets.

At the mere report of me they submit;
sons of foreigners come fawning to me.

The sons of foreigners wither away
and come quaking from their fortresses.

Yahweh lives! Blessed be my rock,
and exalted be the God of my salvation—

the God who gives me vengeance
and subdues peoples under me,

Therefore I will give thanks to you among the nations, Yahweh,
and sing praises to your name.{h}

Great salvation he gives{i} to his king,
and shows covenant love to his anointed,
to David and to his offspring forever.

notes.text: This psalm appears also, with many small differences, in 2 Samuel 22.
This line is not found in 2 Samuel 22.
The horn, the weapon and pride of a strong animal, is a picture of strength and victory.
Hebrew beliyya‘al, “worthlessness,” here perhaps a name for the underworld.
This line is lacking in 2 Samuel 22:14, in some Hebrew manuscripts, and in the Septuagint; it may have been repeated from verse 12.
That is, the enemies.
Or “your humility,” that is, your stooping down; or, as in 2 Samuel 22:36, “your answering.”
Paul quotes this verse in Romans 15:9.
So the qere; the ketiv has “He is a tower of salvation,” as in the qere of 2 Samuel 22:51.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
The heavens are telling the glory of God,
and the expanse{a} proclaims the work of his hands.

Each day gushes forth speech to the next,
and each night makes knowledge known to the next.

There is no speaking and there are no words;
no voice of theirs is heard.

and it is like a bridegroom coming out of his canopy;
like a champion it rejoices to run its path.

Its rising is from the end of the heavens,
and its circuit to their other end,
and there is nothing hidden from its heat.

The law of Yahweh is perfect, restoring the soul;
the testimony of Yahweh is sure, making wise the simple;

the precepts of Yahweh are right, rejoicing the heart;
the commandment of Yahweh is pure, enlightening the eyes;

the fear of Yahweh is clean, enduring forever;
the judgments of Yahweh are true; they are righteous altogether.

More to be desired are they than gold,
even much fine gold;
sweeter also than honey
and the drippings of the honeycomb.

Also by them your servant is made wary;
in the keeping of them there is great reward.

Who can discern his own errors?
Clear me from hidden faults.

Hold back your servant also from willful sins;
do not let them gain mastery over me!
Then I will be whole
and clean of grave transgression.

Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart
be acceptable in your sight,
Yahweh, my rock and my redeemer.

notes.text: Hebrew raqia‘, the vault or dome of the sky (Genesis 1:6–8).
Or “their sound.” The Septuagint has “their sound,” the form quoted in Romans 10:18.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
May Yahweh answer you in the day of trouble!
May the name of the God of Jacob set you on high!

May he send you aid out of the holy place
and uphold you out of Zion!

May he call to mind all your gifts of grain
and accept as rich your burnt offering!
Selah

May he grant you your heart’s desire
and fulfill all your plans!

May we shout for joy over your salvation,
and in the name of our God set up our banners!
May Yahweh fulfill all your requests!

Some trust in chariots and some in horses,
but we will call upon the name of Yahweh our God.

They have buckled and fallen,
but we have stood up and hold our ground.

Yahweh, save the king!{a}
May he answer us in the day we call.

notes.text: Or, following the Septuagint, “Yahweh, save the king, and answer us in the day we call.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
The king shall be glad in your strength, Yahweh,
and how exceedingly he shall rejoice in your salvation!{a}

The longing of his heart you have given him,
and the request of his lips you have not withheld.
Selah

For you come to meet him with rich blessings;
you set a crown of fine gold on his head.

Life he asked of you; you gave it to him,
length of days forever and ever.

Great is his glory through your salvation;
splendor and majesty you lay upon him.

For you make him a blessing forever;
you make him glad with joy in your presence.

For the king trusts in Yahweh,
and through the covenant love of the Most High he shall not be shaken.

Your hand will find out all your enemies;
your right hand will find out those who hate you.

You will make them like a blazing oven
when you appear.{b}
Yahweh will swallow them up in his wrath,
and fire will consume them.

You will destroy their fruit from the earth,
and their offspring from among the children of man.

Though they plan evil against you,
though they devise a scheme, they will not succeed.

For you will make them turn their backs;
you will aim at their faces with your bowstrings.

Be exalted, Yahweh, in your strength!
We will sing and make music to your might.

notes.text: So the qere; the ketiv has a different form of the same verb.
Hebrew “at the time of your face.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader: on “The Doe of the Dawn.”{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
O my God, I cry in the daytime, and you do not hear,
and in the night season, and I am not silent.

But you are holy,
you who inhabit the praises of Israel.

Our fathers trusted in you;
they trusted, and you set them free.

To you they cried and were set free;
in you they trusted and were not put to shame.

But I am a worm, and no man,
a reproach of men and despised of the people.

All who see me mock me;
they curl their lips; they wag their heads:

“He trusted himself to Yahweh;{d} let him deliver him;
let him rescue him, seeing he delights in him!”

Yet you are the one who drew me from the womb;
you made me trust at my mother’s breasts.

On you I was cast from birth;{e}
from my mother’s womb you have been my God.

Be not far from me, for trouble is close at hand,
for there is none to help.

Many bulls encircle me;
strong bulls of Bashan{f} surround me.

They open wide their mouths at me,
a lion tearing and roaring.

My strength is dried up like a potsherd,
and my tongue clings to my jaws,
and you have brought me into the dust of death.

I may tell all my bones;
they look and stare upon me.

they divide my garments among them,
and for my clothing they cast lots.{i}

But you, Yahweh, do not be far off!
O my strength, come quickly to my help!

Deliver my soul from the sword,
my only life{j} from the power of the dog!

Save me from the lion’s mouth!
Even from the horns of the wild oxen you have answered me.{k}

I will declare your name to my brothers;
in the midst of the assembly I will praise you:{l}

For he has not despised nor abhorred
the affliction of the afflicted one;
he has not hidden his face from him,
but when he cried to him, he heard.

My praise shall be of you in the great congregation;
I will pay my vows before those who fear him.

All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to Yahweh,
and all the families of the nations shall bow down before you.{m}

For kingship belongs to Yahweh,
and he rules over the nations.

Offspring shall serve him;
it shall be told of the Lord to the generation to come.{o}

They shall come and proclaim his righteousness
to a people yet to be born,
that he has done it.

notes.text: Hebrew ’ayyelet hashshakhar, probably the name of a tune.
Jesus cried these words from the cross, in Aramaic (Matthew 27:46; Mark 15:34).
Hebrew “my roaring.”
Hebrew “Roll it on Yahweh,” that is, commit your cause to him. Compare Matthew 27:43.
Hebrew “from the womb.”
Bashan, the fertile highlands east of the Sea of Galilee, was famous for its cattle (Amos 4:1).
Hebrew “within my inward parts.”

So some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint (“they dug”), the Syriac, and Jerome (“they bound” or “they pierced”). A Dead Sea Scroll fragment of this psalm from Nahal Hever (5/6HevPs) reads a verb (ka’aru) that may mean “they dug” or “they pierced.” The Masoretic Text reads ka’ari, “like a lion,” which would give “like a lion, my hands and my feet,” a line that lacks a verb and is hard to construe. The difference in the Hebrew is a single letter (waw or yod), which look alike in many scripts. The New Testament gospels do not quote this line, but they describe the crucifixion in words drawn from this psalm (verses 1, 7–8, 18).
See John 19:24 and Matthew 27:35.
Hebrew “my only one,” that is, my precious life.
The sudden “you have answered me” marks the turn from lament to praise. The Septuagint has “and my lowliness from the horns of unicorns.”
Quoted in Hebrews 2:12.
So the Hebrew; some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint, and the Syriac have “before him.”
The Hebrew of this verse is difficult; “the prosperous” is literally “the fat ones.”
Or “to the next generation.” The Hebrew may also be read, with the Septuagint, “and my offspring shall serve him.”

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh is my shepherd;
I shall not be in want.

In grassy pastures he makes me lie down;
beside quiet waters he leads me.{a}

Surely goodness and covenant love shall pursue me
all the days of my life,
and I shall dwell{d} in the house of Yahweh
for length of days.

notes.text: Hebrew “waters of rest.”
Or “in paths of righteousness.”
Or “the valley of the shadow of death.” The Hebrew tsalmawet was understood by ancient translators as “shadow of death”; many scholars read it as “deep darkness.”
So the Septuagint; the Hebrew vowels read “I shall return to.”

chapters.title: Of David. A psalm.

verses.text:
The earth is Yahweh’s, and all that fills it,
the world and those who dwell in it,

for he has founded it upon the seas
and set it firm upon the rivers.

Who shall go up the mountain of Yahweh?
And who shall stand in his holy place?

The one with clean hands and a pure heart,
who has not lifted up his soul{a} to what is false
and has not sworn deceitfully.

He will receive blessing from Yahweh
and righteousness from the God of his salvation.

Lift up your heads, O you gates,
and be lifted up, you everlasting doors,
and the King of glory shall come in.

Who is this King of glory?
Yahweh, strong and mighty,
Yahweh, mighty in battle!

Who is he, this King of glory?
Yahweh of Armies{d}—
he is the King of glory!
Selah

notes.text: So the qere and many manuscripts; the ketiv has “my soul,” that is, “has not taken my name in vain” (compare Exodus 20:7).
So the qere; the ketiv is singular.
So the Septuagint and Syriac; the Hebrew lacks “God of.”
Hebrew YHWH tseba’ot, often rendered “the LORD of hosts.” The “armies” are the hosts of heaven, the angels and stars, and also the armies of Israel.

chapters.title: Of David.{a}

verses.text: To you, Yahweh, I lift up my soul.

Yes, let none who wait on you be ashamed;
let them be ashamed who deal treacherously without cause.

Make me know your ways, Yahweh;
teach me your paths.

Remember your mercy, Yahweh, and your covenant love,
for they have been from of old.

Good and upright is Yahweh;
therefore he instructs sinners in the way.

The meek he will guide in judgment,
and the meek he will teach his way.

All the paths of Yahweh are covenant love and faithfulness
for those who keep his covenant and his testimonies.

For your name’s sake, Yahweh,
pardon my iniquity, for it is great.

Who is the man who fears Yahweh?
Him will he instruct in the way that he should choose.

His soul shall abide in prosperity,
and his offspring shall inherit the land.

The friendship{b} of Yahweh is with those who fear him,
and he will show them his covenant.

My eyes are ever toward Yahweh,
for he will bring my feet out of the net.

Turn yourself to me and have mercy on me,
for I am desolate and afflicted.

The troubles of my heart have grown wide;{c}
bring me out of my distresses.

Look upon my affliction and my pain,
and forgive all my sins.

See how many are my enemies,
and with what violent hatred they hate me.

Guard my soul and deliver me;
let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in you.

May integrity and uprightness preserve me,
for I wait for you.

Redeem Israel, O God,
out of all his troubles.

notes.text: This psalm is an acrostic: each verse begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet, with small irregularities (the letter waw lacks a verse, and qof is replaced). Verse 22 stands outside the pattern.
Or “the secret counsel,” “the intimate circle.”
Or, with a different division of the Hebrew words, “Relieve the troubles of my heart.”

chapters.title: Of David.

verses.text:
Vindicate me, Yahweh, for I have walked in my integrity,
and I have trusted in Yahweh without wavering.

Examine me, Yahweh, and try me;
test my heart and my mind.{a}

For your covenant love is before my eyes,
and I have walked in your truth.

I have not sat with deceitful men,
nor will I go in with pretenders.

I hate the assembly of evildoers,
and with the wicked I will not sit.

I will wash my hands in innocence,
and so will I go about your altar, Yahweh,

that I may make the voice of thanksgiving heard
and tell of all your wondrous works.

Yahweh, I have loved the dwelling of your house
and the place where your glory resides.

Do not gather my soul with sinners,
nor my life with bloodthirsty men,

in whose hands is wickedness,
and their right hand is full of bribes.

But as for me, I will walk in my integrity;
redeem me and have mercy on me.

My foot stands in an even place;
in the congregations I will bless Yahweh.

notes.text: Hebrew “my kidneys and my heart.” “Test” follows the qere; the ketiv has a different form of the verb.

chapters.title: Of David.

verses.text:
When evildoers draw near to me to devour my flesh,
my adversaries and my enemies,
it is they who stumble and fall.

Though an army encamp against me,
my heart shall not fear;
though war rise up against me,
even then I will be confident.

One thing I have asked of Yahweh,
that will I seek:
that I may dwell in the house of Yahweh
all the days of my life,
to behold the beauty of Yahweh
and to inquire{a} in his temple.

Hear, Yahweh, when I cry with my voice;
have mercy also on me and answer me.

When you said, “Seek my face,”{b} my heart said to you,
“Your face, Yahweh, I will seek.”

For my father and my mother have forsaken me,
but Yahweh will take me in.

Teach me your way, Yahweh,
and lead me on a level path
because of those who lie in wait for me.

I believe that I shall see the goodness of Yahweh
in the land of the living!{c}

notes.text: Or “to meditate,” “to seek guidance.”
Hebrew “To you my heart said, ‘Seek my face.’” The sense is uncertain.
The Hebrew begins with a word, “unless,” marked by the Masoretes as doubtful; read with it, “If I had not believed that I would see…” The word is lacking in the Septuagint.

chapters.title: Of David.

verses.text:
To you, Yahweh, I call;
my rock, do not be deaf to me,
lest, if you are silent to me,
I become like those who go down to the pit.

Hear the voice of my supplications
when I cry to you,
when I lift up my hands
toward your holy inner sanctuary.{a}

Do not draw me away with the wicked
and with those who work iniquity,
who speak peace to their neighbors,
but mischief is in their hearts.

Because they do not regard the works of Yahweh
or the work of his hands,
he will tear them down and not build them up.

Blessed be Yahweh!
For he has heard the voice of my pleas for mercy.

Yahweh is strength to his people,{b}
and he is the saving strength of his anointed.

Save your people, and bless your inheritance;
shepherd them also, and lift them up forever.

notes.text: Hebrew debir, the innermost room of the temple, the Most Holy Place.
So some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint, and the Syriac; most Hebrew manuscripts have “their strength.”

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Ascribe to Yahweh, you sons of God,{a}
ascribe to Yahweh glory and strength.

Ascribe to Yahweh the glory due his name;
worship Yahweh in the splendor of holiness.{b}

The voice of Yahweh is powerful;
the voice of Yahweh is full of majesty.

The voice of Yahweh breaks the cedars;
Yahweh breaks the cedars of Lebanon.

He makes them also to skip like a calf,
Lebanon and Sirion{c} like a young wild ox.
The voice of Yahweh splits flames of fire.

The voice of Yahweh shakes the wilderness;
Yahweh shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.

Yahweh sat enthroned over the flood;{e}
Yahweh sits enthroned as King forever.

May Yahweh give strength to his people!
May Yahweh bless his people with peace!

notes.text: Hebrew bene ’elim, “sons of gods,” the heavenly beings around God’s throne.
Or “in holy attire.”
Sirion is the Sidonian name for Mount Hermon (Deuteronomy 3:9).
Or, with a slight change, “twists the oaks.”
Hebrew mabbul, used elsewhere only of Noah’s flood (Genesis 6–11).

chapters.title: A psalm. A song at the dedication of the house.{a} Of David.

verses.text:
I will exalt you, Yahweh, for you have drawn me up
and have not let my foes rejoice over me.

Yahweh my God, I cried to you,
and you have healed me.

Yahweh, you have brought up my soul from Sheol;
you have kept me alive, so that I did not go down to the pit.{b}

Sing praises to Yahweh, you his faithful ones,
and give thanks to his holy name.{c}

For his anger is but for a moment,
and his favor is for a lifetime.
Weeping may tarry for the night,
but joy comes with the morning.

As for me, I said in my prosperity,
“I shall never be moved.”

Yahweh, by your favor you made my mountain stand strong;
you hid your face; I was dismayed.

To you, Yahweh, I cried,
and to the Lord I pleaded for mercy:

“What gain is there in my blood
when I go down to the pit?
Shall the dust praise you?
Shall it declare your truth?

Hear, Yahweh, and be gracious to me!
Yahweh, be my helper!”

You have turned my mourning into dancing for me;
you have loosed my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness,

so that my glory{d} may sing praise to you and not be silent.
Yahweh my God, I will give thanks to you forever!

notes.text: Perhaps the temple, or David’s palace; Jewish tradition has used this psalm at Hanukkah, the feast of the rededication of the temple.
So the qere; the ketiv has “from among those who go down to the pit.”
Hebrew “to the remembrance of his holiness.”
That is, my soul, or my whole being.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Bow down your ear to me;
rescue me speedily!
Be my strong rock,
a fortress to save me.

For you are my crag and my fortress;
therefore for your name’s sake lead me and guide me.

Pull me out of the net that they have hidden for me,
for you are my stronghold.

Into your hand I commit my spirit;{a}
you have redeemed me, Yahweh, God of truth.

I hate those who cling to worthless idols,{b}
but I trust in Yahweh.

and you have not shut me up in the hand of the enemy;
you have set my feet in a broad place.

Because of all my foes I have become a reproach,
above all to my neighbors,
and a fear to those who know me;
those who see me outside run from me.

I am forgotten like a dead man, out of mind;
I have become like a broken vessel.

For I have heard the whispering of many—
terror on every side!—
while they plot together against me,
they scheme to take away my life.

But I trusted in you, Yahweh;
I said, “You are my God.”

My times are in your hand;
deliver me from the hand of my enemies and from those who persecute me!

Let your face shine on your servant;
save me for your covenant love’s sake.

Let the lying lips be struck dumb,
which speak arrogantly against the righteous
in pride and contempt.

Oh, how abundant is your goodness,
which you have laid up for those who fear you
and worked for those who take refuge in you
before the children of man!

You hide them in the secret of your presence
from the schemes of men;
you keep them secretly in a booth
from the strife of tongues.

Blessed be Yahweh,
for he has shown me his marvelous covenant love
in a besieged city.

As for me, I said in my alarm,
“I am cut off from before your eyes.”
Nevertheless you heard the voice of my supplications
when I cried to you.

Love Yahweh, all you his faithful ones!
Yahweh preserves the faithful
and repays in full the one who acts proudly.

Be strong, and let your heart take courage,
all you who hope in Yahweh!

notes.text: Jesus spoke these words as he died (Luke 23:46).
Hebrew “vanities of emptiness.” So the Septuagint and some Hebrew manuscripts; the Masoretic Text has “I hate.”
The Septuagint and Syriac have “because of my affliction.”

chapters.title: Of David. A Maskil.{a}

verses.text:
Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven,
whose sin is covered.{b}

Blessed is the man to whom Yahweh does not count iniquity,
and in whose spirit there is no deceit.

When I kept silent, my bones wasted away
through my groaning all day long.

I acknowledged my sin to you,
and my iniquity I did not hide;
I said, “I will confess my transgressions to Yahweh,”
and you forgave the iniquity of my sin.
Selah

Therefore let everyone who is faithful pray to you
at a time when you may be found;{d}
surely in the flood of great waters
they shall not reach him.

I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go;
I will counsel you with my eye upon you.

Do not be like the horse or like the mule, without understanding,
whose trappings must be bit and bridle to hold them in,
or they will not come near you.

Many are the sorrows of the wicked,
but covenant love surrounds the one who trusts in Yahweh.

Be glad in Yahweh and rejoice, you righteous,
and shout for joy, all you upright in heart!

notes.text: Hebrew maskil, a term of uncertain meaning found in thirteen psalm titles; perhaps “a skillful psalm” or “an instructive psalm” (compare verse 8, “I will instruct you,” from the same root).
Verses 1–2 are quoted in Romans 4:7–8.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Hebrew “at a time of finding.” The sense is uncertain.

verses.text:
Shout for joy in Yahweh, O you righteous!
Praise is fitting for the upright.

Give thanks to Yahweh with the lyre;
make music to him with the ten-stringed harp!

Sing to him a new song;
play skillfully with a loud shout.

For the word of Yahweh is upright,
and all his work is done in faithfulness.

He loves righteousness and justice;
the earth is full of the covenant love of Yahweh.

By the word of Yahweh the heavens came to be,
and all their array by the breath of his mouth.

He gathers the waters of the sea as a heap;{a}
he lays up the deeps in storehouses.

Let all the earth fear Yahweh;
let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him.

For he spoke, and it was;
he commanded, and it stood firm.

Yahweh brings the counsel of the nations to nothing;
he frustrates the devices of the peoples.

The counsel of Yahweh stands forever,
the thoughts of his heart to all generations.

Blessed is the nation whose God is Yahweh,
the people he has chosen as his heritage!

Yahweh looks down from heaven;
he beholds all the children of man;

from the place of his dwelling he gazes
on all the inhabitants of the earth,

he who fashions the hearts of them all
and discerns all their deeds.

No king is saved by the size of his army;
a mighty man is not delivered by great strength.

A horse is a false hope for safety;
for all its great strength it will not deliver.

Behold, the eye of Yahweh is on those who fear him,
on those who hope in his covenant love,

to deliver their soul from death
and to keep them alive in famine.

Our soul waits for Yahweh;
he is our help and our shield.

For our heart shall rejoice in him,
because we have trusted in his holy name.

Let your covenant love, Yahweh, rest upon us,
just as we have hoped in you.

notes.text: Or, with the ancient versions, “as in a skin bottle.”

chapters.title: Of David, when he disguised his sanity before Abimelech,{a} who drove him away, and he departed.

verses.text:
I will bless Yahweh at all times;
his praise shall continually be in my mouth.

My soul shall make its boast in Yahweh;
let the humble hear and be glad.

Oh, magnify Yahweh with me,
and let us exalt his name together!

I sought Yahweh, and he answered me
and delivered me from all my terrors.

Those who looked to him were radiant,{b}
and their faces were never ashamed.

This poor man cried, and Yahweh heard him
and saved him out of all his troubles.

The angel of Yahweh encamps around those who fear him,
and he rescues them.

Taste and see that Yahweh is good!{c}
Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him!

Fear Yahweh, you his saints,
for there is no want to those who fear him.

The young lions suffer want and hunger,
but those who seek Yahweh shall not lack any good thing.

Come, you children, listen to me;
I will teach you the fear of Yahweh.

Who is the man who desires life
and loves many days, that he may see good?{d}

Keep your tongue from evil
and your lips from speaking deceit.

Turn away from evil and do good;
seek peace and pursue it.

The eyes of Yahweh are toward the righteous,
and his ears are open to their cry.

The face of Yahweh is against those who do evil,
to cut off the memory of them from the earth.

The righteous cry,{e} and Yahweh hears
and delivers them out of all their troubles.

Yahweh is close to those of a broken heart
and saves such as are of a crushed spirit.

Many are the afflictions of the righteous,
but Yahweh delivers him out of them all.

He keeps all his bones;
not one of them is broken.{f}

Evil shall slay the wicked,
and those who hate the righteous shall be held guilty.

Yahweh redeems the soul of his servants;
none of those who take refuge in him shall be held guilty.

notes.text: This psalm is an acrostic, each verse beginning with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet; the letter waw is lacking, and verse 22 stands outside the pattern (as in Psalm 25). The title recalls 1 Samuel 21:10–15, where the king of Gath is named Achish; Abimelech may have been a royal title among the Philistines (compare Genesis 20; 26).
So the Hebrew; some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint, and the Syriac have “Look to him and be radiant, and your faces shall not be ashamed.”
Compare 1 Peter 2:3.
Verses 12–16 are quoted in 1 Peter 3:10–12.
Hebrew “They cry.”
Compare John 19:36.

chapters.title: Of David.

verses.text:
Contend, Yahweh, with those who contend with me;
fight against those who fight against me!

Take hold of shield and buckler
and rise up for my help!

Draw out the spear and the battle-ax{a} against my pursuers!
Say to my soul, “I am your salvation!”

Let those who seek my life
be confounded and put to shame!
Let those who plot my harm
be turned back and brought to confusion!

May they be as chaff before the wind,
the angel of Yahweh thrusting them on!

Let their way be dark and slippery,
with the angel of Yahweh pursuing them!

For they hid their net for me in a pit without cause;
without cause they dug for my soul.

Then my soul will rejoice in Yahweh,
exulting in his salvation.

All my bones shall say,
“Yahweh, who is like you,
delivering the poor from him who is too strong for him,
the poor and needy from him who robs him?”

Malicious witnesses rise up;
they ask me of things that I do not know.

They paid me back evil for good,
leaving my soul forlorn.{b}

like godless jesters mocking for a cake,{d}
they ground their teeth at me.

Lord, how long will you look on?
Rescue my soul from their ravages,
my only life{e} from the lions!

I will give you thanks in the great congregation;
among a mighty people I will praise you.

Do not let those who are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me,
nor let those who hate me without cause wink the eye.{f}

For they do not speak peace,
but they devise deceitful words
against those who are quiet in the land.

Yes, they opened their mouth wide against me
and said, “Aha, aha, our eye has seen it!”

You have seen, Yahweh; do not keep silent!
Lord, be not far from me!

Rouse yourself, awake for my justice,
for my cause, my God and my Lord!

Vindicate me, Yahweh my God, according to your righteousness,
and let them not rejoice over me!

Let them not say in their heart, “Aha, so would we have it!”
Let them not say, “We have devoured him.”

Let them be ashamed and confounded together
who rejoice at my calamity!
Let them be clothed with shame and dishonor
who magnify themselves against me!

Then my tongue will utter your righteousness,
your praise, the whole day through.

notes.text: Or “and close the way.”
Hebrew “bereavement to my soul.”
Perhaps meaning that he prayed with his head bowed upon his chest, or that his prayer was in vain.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Hebrew “my only one,” as in Psalm 22:20.
Compare John 15:25, “They hated me without a cause.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader. Of David, the servant of Yahweh.

verses.text:
For he flatters himself in his own eyes
that his iniquity will not be found out and hated.

The words of his mouth are wickedness and deceit;
he has ceased to act wisely and to do good.

Your covenant love, Yahweh, reaches to the heavens,
your faithfulness to the clouds.

How precious is your covenant love, O God!
The children of man take refuge in the shadow of your wings.

They shall be filled to the full with the fatness of your house,
and you will make them drink of the river of your delights.{c}

For with you is the fountain of life;
in your light we see light.

Continue your covenant love to those who know you,
and your righteousness to the upright in heart!

Let not the foot of the proud come upon me,
nor the hand of the wicked drive me away.

There the workers of iniquity have fallen;
they are thrust down and cannot rise.

notes.text: So some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint, and the Syriac; most Hebrew manuscripts have “my heart.” Hebrew “An oracle of transgression to the wicked.”
Quoted in Romans 3:18.
Hebrew ‘adanekha, from the same root as “Eden.”

chapters.title: Of David.{a}

verses.text:
Do not fret yourself because of evildoers,
nor be envious of those who work unrighteousness!

For like the grass they will soon wither
and fade like the green herb.

Trust in Yahweh and do good;
dwell in the land and feed on faithfulness.{b}

Take delight in Yahweh,
and he will give you the requests of your heart.

Roll your way onto Yahweh;
trust in him, and he will act.

He will make your righteousness go forth as the light,
and your just cause as the noon.

Leave off from anger and let go of wrath!
Do not fret yourself; it tends only to evil.

For evildoers shall be cut off,
but those who wait for Yahweh shall inherit the land.

For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be;
yes, you shall diligently consider his place, and it shall not be.

But the meek shall inherit the land{c}
and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.

The wicked schemes against the just
and gnashes on him with his teeth.

but the Lord laughs at him,
for he sees that his day is coming.

their sword shall enter their own heart,
and their bows shall be broken.

Better is the little that the righteous has
than the abundance of many wicked.

For the arms of the wicked shall be broken,
but Yahweh upholds the righteous.

Yahweh knows the days of the upright,
and their inheritance shall be forever.

they will not be put to shame in the evil time;
in the days of famine they will have plenty.

The wicked borrows and pays not back again,
but the righteous shows mercy and gives.

for those blessed by him{e} shall inherit the land,
but those cursed by him shall be cut off.

The steps of a man are established by Yahweh
when he delights in his way;

though he falls, he shall not be cast headlong,
for Yahweh holds his hand.

I have been young, and now am old,
yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken
or his children begging for bread.

All the day long he is gracious and lends,
and his children become a blessing.

Depart from evil and do good,
and dwell forevermore.

The righteous shall inherit the land
and dwell upon it forever.

The righteous man’s mouth murmurs wisdom,
and his tongue speaks what is just.

The law of his God is in his heart;
his steps do not slip.

The wicked keeps watch on the righteous
and seeks to kill him.

Yahweh will not leave him in his hand,
nor condemn him when he is judged.

I have seen the wicked in great power,
spreading himself like a green tree in its native soil.{g}

Yet he passed away,{h} and lo, he was not;
yes, I sought him, but he could not be found.

Mark the blameless and behold the upright,
for there is a future{i} for the man of peace.

But transgressors shall be destroyed together;
the future of the wicked shall be cut off.

The salvation of the righteous is from Yahweh;
he is their stronghold in the time of trouble.

notes.text: This psalm is an acrostic: every second verse, roughly, begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet, so that each letter introduces a stanza of about two verses.
Or “and befriend faithfulness,” or “and you shall feed securely.”
Compare Matthew 5:5.
Or “like the burning of furnaces.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
That is, by Yahweh.
The ayin stanza appears here; the Septuagint has “The lawless shall be driven out,” which some take to preserve the letter.
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint has “like the cedars of Lebanon.”
So the Septuagint, Syriac, and Vulgate; the Hebrew has “he passed away” in some manuscripts and “one passed by” in others.
Or “posterity.”

chapters.title: A psalm of David, for the memorial offering.{a}

verses.text:
Yahweh, do not rebuke me in your wrath,
nor chasten me in your hot displeasure.

For your arrows stick fast in me,
and your hand presses me down.

There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation;
there is no health in my bones because of my sin.

For my iniquities have gone over my head;
like a heavy burden, they are too heavy for me.

My wounds reek and are rotten
because of my foolishness.

I am bent and bowed down greatly;
all the day I go about mourning.

For my loins are filled with burning,
and there is no soundness in my flesh.

I am feeble and utterly crushed;
I groan because of the turmoil of my heart.

Lord, all my desire is before you,
and my groaning is not hidden from you.

My heart pants; my strength fails me;
as for the light of my eyes, it also is gone from me.

My loved ones and my friends stand aloof from my plague,
and my kinsmen stand far off.

But I am like the deaf; I hear nothing,
like the dumb, who opens not his mouth.

Thus I am as a man who hears not,
in whose mouth are no reproofs.

But for you, Yahweh, I wait;
it is you who will answer, Lord my God.

For I said, “Let them not rejoice over me,
who magnify themselves against me when my foot slips!”

For I am ready to stumble,
and my pain is ever before me.

For I will declare my iniquity;
I am troubled over my sin.

But my enemies are vigorous; they are strong,{b}
and many are those who hate me wrongfully.

They also who render evil for good are my adversaries,
because I follow what is good.{c}

Do not forsake me, Yahweh!
My God, be not far from me!

Make haste to help me,
Lord, my salvation!

notes.text: Hebrew lehazkir, “to bring to remembrance.” The same word appears in the title of Psalm 70; it may refer to the memorial portion of the grain offering (Leviticus 2:2).
Hebrew “my enemies are living.” A Dead Sea Scroll (4QPs-a) reads “without cause,” matching the parallel line.
So the qere; the ketiv has a different form of the same word.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: for Jeduthun.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
I said, “I will take heed to my ways,
that I do not sin with my tongue;
I will keep a bridle on my mouth
while the wicked is before me.”

“Yahweh, cause me to know my end,
and the measure of my days, what it is,
that I may know how frail I am.

Behold, you have made my days as handbreadths,{c}
and my lifetime is as nothing before you.
Surely every man, even standing firm, is altogether breath.
Selah

“And now, Lord, what do I wait for?
My hope is in you.

Rescue me from all my transgressions;
do not set me up as the taunt of the fool.

I was dumb; I opened not my mouth,
because you did it.

Remove your stroke from me;
I am consumed by the blow of your hand.

When with rebukes you correct a man for iniquity,
you make his beauty consume away like a moth;
surely every man is a breath.
Selah

Turn your gaze from me, that I may brighten,
before I go hence and be no more.”

notes.text: So the qere; the ketiv spells the name Jedithun. Jeduthun was one of David’s chief musicians (1 Chronicles 16:41–42; 25:1). The name is also in the titles of Psalms 62 and 77.
Hebrew “away from good.”
A handbreadth is about 7.5 centimeters (3 inches). Hebrew hebel, “breath, vapor,” is the word rendered “vanity” in Ecclesiastes.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. Of David. A psalm.

verses.text:
I waited patiently for Yahweh;
he inclined to me and heard my cry.

He brought me up out of a horrible pit,{a}
out of the miry clay,
and set my feet upon a rock
and established my goings.

And he has put a new song in my mouth,
praise to our God;
many shall see it and fear
and shall trust in Yahweh.

Blessed is the man who makes Yahweh his trust,
and does not regard the proud,
nor such as turn aside to lies.

Then I said, “Lo, I come;
in the scroll of the book it is written of me:

I delight to do your will, O my God;
yes, your law is within my inmost parts.”

As for you, Yahweh, you will not withhold your mercy from me;
your covenant love and your truth will ever preserve me!

Be pleased, Yahweh, to deliver me!{c}
Yahweh, make haste to help me!

Let them be ashamed and confounded together
who seek after my soul to destroy it;
let them be driven backward and put to shame
who wish me evil.

Let them be desolate as a reward for their shame
who say to me, “Aha, aha!”

Let all who seek you
rejoice and be glad in you;
let such as love your salvation
say continually, “Yahweh be magnified!”

notes.text: Or “the pit of tumult.”
Hebrew “ears you have dug for me.” The Septuagint has “but a body you have prepared for me,” the reading quoted in Hebrews 10:5–7.
Verses 13–17 appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 70.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Blessed is he who considers the poor!
Yahweh will deliver him in the time of trouble;

Yahweh will strengthen him upon the bed of languishing;
you will make all his bed in his sickness.{b}

As for me, I said, “Yahweh, be gracious to me;
heal my soul, for I have sinned against you!”

My enemies speak evil of me:
“When shall he die and his name perish?”

All who hate me whisper together against me;
against me they devise my hurt.

“A thing of ruin,”{c} they say, “clings fast to him;
and now that he lies down he shall rise up no more.”

But you, Yahweh, be gracious to me,
and raise me up, that I may repay them!

By this I know that you favor me,
because my enemy does not triumph over me.

And as for me, you uphold me in my integrity
and set me before your face forever.

notes.text: So the qere; the ketiv has “and may he be called blessed.”
Hebrew “all his bed you turn over in his illness.”
Hebrew “a thing of Belial,” that is, of worthlessness or ruin.
Hebrew “the man of my peace.” Quoted by Jesus of Judas in John 13:18.
This doxology closes Book One of the Psalms (Psalms 1–41). Each of the five books ends with a similar blessing (41:13; 72:18–19; 89:52; 106:48), and Psalm 150 closes the whole.
